items.title: Sherwood Mangiapane Interview, 1959-05-05
items.q: I was playing with Classy when he loaned me that bass, and I started to play the thing in his band.

ctx.x: And when you took up your string bass, which band did you belong to first?
Classy. Same thing? I was playing with Classy when he loaned me that bass, and I started to play the thing in his band.
Do you remember some of the jobs you played in different places, aside from parties?

items.title: Sherwood Mangiapane Interview, 1959-05-05
items.q: he said to me one night... he said, I have one. Come get it and take it home

ctx.x: N.J. Nick. Nick Klessy, I think.

Nick Klessy, I think. I think he was a realtor. I couldn't say. I don't know. But anyhow, Joe Klessy was the type of guy that would give you the shirt off his back. And he said to me one night, I was playing sousaphone then, only the sousaphone, he said, Why don't you get a string bass? Well in those days you'd play all night for three bucks, you know, and nobody could afford two or three instruments. I was paying for a bass on at the time and I told him, Well I can't afford that. And I don't know if I'd have the…
Did you start bowing on it or picking?
